title: Keypad Digits to Letter Strings
statement:
On an old phone keypad, each digit from 2 to 9 stands for some letters:

2 → abc, 3 → def, 4 → ghi, 5 → jkl, 6 → mno, 7 → pqrs, 8 → tuv, 9 → wxyz.

You get a string digits of such digits. Return every string you can get by replacing each digit with one of its letters. The strings may be returned in any order. If digits is empty, return an empty list, not a list holding the empty string.

examples.why: 7 and 9 each have four letters, so 4 × 4 = 16 strings, not 3 × 3.
One digit: one string per letter.
No digits gives no strings. Returning [""] is the common slip.

constraints: digits[i] is a digit from 2 to 9
hints: Fix a letter for the first digit. What is left is the same problem for the remaining digits.
Build the string position by position: at index i, try each letter of digits[i] in turn.
Recurse with an index i. If i equals the length, record the current string. Otherwise, for each letter of digits[i]: append it, recurse with i + 1, remove it. Handle the empty input before starting.

explain.intuition:
The same template with the simplest tree of all. Level i of the tree belongs to digit i, and each node has one child per letter of that digit. Every choice is independent: there is no start index to track, nothing to skip, and no branch is ever a dead end. Every leaf at depth digits.length is an answer, so the answer count is the product of the letter counts, at most 4⁴ = 256.

The one trap is the empty input. The recursion records a string when it reaches depth digits.length; for an empty input that is depth 0, so it would record "" and return [""]. Check for empty input first and return [].
steps: go(i): if i === digits.length, record the joined letters and return.
For each letter of KEYS[digits[i]]: push it, call go(i + 1), pop.
pitfalls: Giving every digit three letters. 7 and 9 have four, so "79" has 16 answers.
Building strings with cur + letter and also pushing to a shared array. Use one approach: either pass a new string down, or push and pop.

solutions.title: Backtracking over the digits
solutions.idea: One level per digit, one branch per letter. Record the string at the bottom.

solutions.title: Grow the list digit by digit
solutions.idea: Start with [""]. For each digit, replace every string so far with one copy per letter of that digit.

followups: Only strings that are real words in a given dictionary should be returned. How can the dictionary prune the search early?
Return the k-th string in alphabetical order without building the others.
lcTitle: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
